questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Berkeley because I wanted to learn more about fluid mechanics, which is something NBI doesn't have a lot of courses in. I also wanted to do a project abroad and get new connections for future research purposes.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Absolutely great. I really enjoyed living in "International House". The vibrant atmosphere of the Berkeley campus is really fun, and I've gotten a lot of new friendships with people all over the world. I have learn't a lot from the (very challenging) classes in the physics program. I also chose to do a research project at UC Berkeley, which I can really recommend as it contributes to my international network.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I thought it was mostly pretty easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: No assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Personally, I didn't participate in the orientation, but I heard people who did got a lot out of it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think finding housing is relatively easy - at least for me. I applied to Berkeley Coops, and to International-House. I ended up getting offers from both, and chose International-House, which has been great!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live close to the hills. It is a safe and beautiful area. Not too much noise either.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Registration process is a bit difficult. I had to email a bounch of professors to be allowed to take certain courses, and I had to be on waitlists sometimes.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On the undergrad program, you can enrol in any undergrad course in the department, but you have to be fast for certain courses, since they fill up. If so, you would have to get on a waitlist. For graduate classes or classes outside the department, you can sometimes be lucky to get permission to enroll by asking the professor of the class.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The professors are usually helpful. You can attend the first lecture of the class, and the ask the professor if there are any options for enrolling.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly very succesfull. One class was super hard to get a spot for, but the professor was helpful in talking to the department to get me a permission to take it (it was a graduate class). Another class I wasn't allowed to take (in the EECS-department) since they only take full-time students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in good time, and check in with the professor if the class is right for you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super challenging, but very insightful.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some classes are extremely challenging, so it might be a good idea to try to connect with students who have taken it previously to get an idea of the level. Also be sure to take some more low-effort classes to dilute the challenging ones as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are only office hours where you can come and ask questions to a professor or TA. There are no "regnøvelser" (theoretical exercise). Also, the classes have no breaks. They are just 90 minutes with no breaks.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CHM ENG 299 Chemical Engineering Graduate research
PHYS 212 Advanced Statistical Physics
CHM ENG 250 Transport Phenomena

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
CHM ENG 299 Chemical Engineering Graduate research
MATH 228B Numerical Solution of differential equations
MENG 260B Advanced fluid mechanics 2

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For masters level physics students CHM ENG 250 Transport Phenomena is a great course in continuum mechanics and fluid mechanics - although very challenging. The courses MATH 228B Numerical Solution of differential equations and MENG 260B Advanced fluid mechanics 2 are also great - although not as challenging. I can also recommend to do research projects for units, which I have done. But be careful with the graduate physics classes - they can be pretty hard.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was supposed to bring my own blanket and pillow for living in I-house.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is relatively inexpensive, except living costs and food.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I participated in the UC Berkeley Taekwondo club and there are a million other clubs as well.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are free gyms. Personally I spent a lot of time at I-houses "diversiteas" which are culture nights at I-house with a specific country each wednesday.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get to know some of the trails in the hills – like the fire trails. The nature is very nice. I can defninently also recommend the Taekwondo club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If they actually have time to do so, I would recommend renting cars and exploring the nature in the bay area.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Mostly very easy I would say. People are very friendly and talkative.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club. Join the golden bear orientation. Try to live in a coop or in International House.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are not very humble, and talk a lot about their achievements compared to Europeans, but this doesn't mean they are being full of themselves necessarily. It is mostly a cultural difference.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked that the campus culture is so extremely diverese, and ambitious. Also most people are very friendly and talkative.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be in good time with enrolling in classes and writing to professors. Don't take too hard classes. Try to live in a place with other people that are not much younger than yourself - this could be International House or a coop (UC Berkeley Coops).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sent an application to I-house or UC Berkeley coops as soon as you get your student ID. This will increase your chances of getting a place there. Make sure to notify the coop that you are an international student (This doesn't happen automatically) so that they will give you prioritisation. These places are great to live in!!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I learned a lot about my area of academic interest: fluid mechanics, and that I have gotten a much larger international research network.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: How hard the classes were.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
